### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s).

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 862f12c0b9b36a6192f6ffe55f4052fa7dbaf34a`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 862f12c0b9b36a6192f6ffe55f4052fa7dbaf34a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `73a9844f1ca78d9624c637b2a4b620753649c059` — the merge of head `ee558beae293d714607d1162d6586bbf9c29c9da` into base `862f12c0b9b36a6192f6ffe55f4052fa7dbaf34a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 73a9844f1ca78d9624c637b2a4b620753649c059 && git checkout 73a9844f1ca78d9624c637b2a4b620753649c059
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 862f12c0b9b36a6192f6ffe55f4052fa7dbaf34a ee558beae293d714607d1162d6586bbf9c29c9da && git checkout -B drift-repro 862f12c0b9b36a6192f6ffe55f4052fa7dbaf34a && git merge --no-ff ee558beae293d714607d1162d6586bbf9c29c9da

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 862f12c0b9b36a6192f6ffe55f4052fa7dbaf34a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 862f12c0b9b36a6192f6ffe55f4052fa7dbaf34a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ee558beae293d714607d1162d6586bbf9c29c9da`
Local-runs: none

Scope read: PR #21179 at the head above (a merge commit; the diff judged is the three-dot diff against the merge base, which the compare endpoint reports as the PR's base sha), 11 files, +2336 / −12, head repo equal to base repo; card #21154's body and all eight comments; #21080's ACCEPT `5931764832`; the head's 42 check-runs, 0 failed (skipped by design: Console Pin Gate, the opt-in packed-tarball smoke, and superseded Auto Label / Check PR Size runs). ⚠️ Classes and positions only: no column spelling, probe value or returned value below.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set change the diff implies is a narrowing on an engine read middleware, judged against triage's ruling `5929903631` (option A), the claim amendment `5931964383` and the seat's decisions `5933122330`:

1. **Activity stream, three value-bearing columns (the text, the record label, the recorded change)** — `plugin-audit/src/parent-field-query-guard.ts`, `ACTIVITY_QUERY_GUARD`, registered by `installParentFieldQueryGuards` from `AuditPlugin` with one call. For a non-system caller on `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate`, a query naming one of them as a condition key or cross-field comparand in the filter or in `having`, as a sort field, as a grouping key, or as an aggregation's field or filter is refused unless the caller is served every field of the objects the query can reach. **Right.** The column list equals the redaction's own fail-closed strip, and `activity-predicate-guard.test.ts` pins the two lists equal.
2. **Compliance ledger, the two before/after snapshot columns** — same module, `AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_GUARD`, same clause set and ops. **Right** (seat 2's member, `5931903481`). The list equals the ledger redaction's private snapshot-column constant at this head; the ledger's own metadata column is written only by the auth-event writer and carries no parent field value, so the two snapshot columns are the ledger's whole value-bearing set. ⚠️ Unlike the activity list, nothing pins this list equal to `redactAuditLogRows`'s strip — F11 below.
3. **Approval request, the snapshot column** — `plugin-approvals/src/payload-predicate-guard.ts`, `bindSnapshotPredicateGuard`, registered beside the snapshot redaction in `ApprovalsServicePlugin.start`, same clause set and ops. **Right** — this is #21080's finding (a), folded here as its ACCEPT said it would be.
4. **Which caller is admitted.** A pinned query (one parent or subject named by equality on the parent-object column at the filter's root or inside a root conjunction, machine-name shaped, not the guarded object itself) is admitted iff the serve seam's served set (`resolveServedFields` / `resolveReadableSnapshotFields`, asked as the caller) lacks no field of the security service's read projection asked as the system. An unpinned query is admitted iff that holds for every object `registry.getAllObjects()` returns. **Right.** The declared set is read from metadata, never from rows, so it is the same for a matching and a non-matching probe; the per-object question is the redactions' own composition, so masking is not derived a second time; the refusal names only the columns the query named. No oracle.
5. **Fail-closed arms.** An engine that cannot list its objects (member absent, throws, or an empty list) refuses; a security answer whose system-side projection cannot be had refuses; an exception inside the judgement refuses with a warning. A serve seam that answers "no answer" (no security service, or an object it cannot resolve) admits — the same arm the redactions take, so the predicate discloses nothing the served rows do not. **Right.**
6. **Membership pins and alternatives are not pins** (`$in`, a parent named only inside `$or` or `$not`, two different parents): judged as unpinned. **Right** — admitting them would widen; pinned in both unit suites.
7. **Doors.** `ObjectQL.executeWithMiddleware` is dispatched by exactly find, findOne, insert, update, delete, count and aggregate, in registration order, so the four read ops are the whole engine read set; a free-text search is expanded into the filter before the chain on find, findOne and aggregate, and `count`'s AST carries the filter only; an array-shaped filter is lowered, or refused as malformed, by `lowerWhereFilterArray` ahead of the chain on all four read verbs. The activity guard registers before the read gate, so a refused query pays no pre-scan. System-context and context-less calls are skipped, as the redactions skip them. The analytics door reaches these objects through the engine since #21080, which this head merges. **Right** — no engine door escapes.
8. **Refusal shape.** Code `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `status` and `statusCode` 403, the engine's `details.reason`, and a first sentence byte-equal to plugin-security's predicate guard (filter, sort and search roles) or aggregate-input guard (grouping and aggregation roles), followed by one remedy sentence naming the rule and nothing about the parent's fields. **Right.**
9. **Public surface.** Neither package's `index.ts` changes; both `exports` maps expose the entry only, so the new modules and their exports are unreachable from the package entry — no published accept set widens and nothing new is published. The declaration's `no` value is **right**.
10. **Census page** `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: rows 17 and 45 gain the two guards' registration anchors and extend their behaviour prose to the anchors; six derived counts move. The population gate `check:system-context-census` runs in Lint & Repo Gates, green on this head, so the counts are the generator's. **Right** — not a published surface.
11. **Nothing widens** against the merge base: every query main answers that this head refuses is a narrowing, and the admission arm admits a subset of what main admits.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/21154-activity-text-predicate.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-audit` **minor**, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` **minor**, both published packages. BREAKING is carried by the `!` in the title, the `**BREAKING**` banner and the `(narrowing)` arm — the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major`: no `major`; breaking-ness on its carriers). **Matches what the diff publishes:** a runtime accept-set narrowing in both packages, no new published key.
- The declaration line reads `no (narrowing)` on PR body line 2 and in the changeset body. The grammar is legal (a `no` value with the narrowing arm) and the arm is the right one: the value answers whether the card widens an accept set or enlarges the public surface (it does not); the arm records the direction (it narrows). The claim's own expectation of `no (narrowing)` is met.
- One ADR-0087 marker, category `no-migration-prescription`, with its why. Nothing authorable changes spelling or shape; the body carries no FROM → TO rewrite, no migration-framed table and no removal instruction — the one-line-fix paragraph prescribes a query shape, not a rewrite of a consumer's code. The per-PR Check Changeset job, which runs the empty-changeset, ADR-0087 and no-major gates against the merge base, concludes success on this head.
- Consumer text: who is affected (by caller class), what is refused (by clause), what is unchanged, and the one-line fix are all stated. **Consistent.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F1 — round-0 Q1, the unpinned rule** (`5933075511`, decided in `5933122330`): built as the declared set (D). Judged right in ① 4–5. The seat's three pins are present: admin controls in all three unit suites and both dogfood files; each restricted class refused pinned and unpinned; an admission-arm ablation reported turning exactly the seven admin and control pins red. **Answered.**
- **F2 — round-0 Q2, the census anchors**: carried here; the gate is green. **Answered.**
- **F3 — the analytics native path** (round-0 out-of-scope finding): #21080 is merged into this head; the engine `aggregate` refusal is pinned here and the routing is pinned in #21080's own PR, so the reading closes by construction. The dev's post-merge re-measurement is private and was not an input. **Accepted on construction.**
- **F4 — cost of the admission** (round-1 finding, carrier none): three security-service calls per registered object per unpinned query, uncached across queries, paid in full only by a caller who is admitted; a restricted caller stops at the first withholding object; a pinned query pays three. The stated cost matches the code. **Accepted.**
- **F5 — the fixture pin's premise** (deviation): the dogfood fixture's admin lacked the fixture's two capability sets and was refused correctly; the correction grants them in the fixture, the guard is unchanged, and the prediction was re-recorded. **Accepted.**
- **F6 — the clause walk restated in both plugins** (carrier none): compared clause by clause with plugin-security's `collectQueryFields` and `collectConditionFields` — the same three logical keys, the same comparand reading through `FieldReferenceSchema`, the same head-segment rule, the same sort, grouping and aggregation handling, projection excluded. Equal today. ⚠️ Three copies now exist with no pin across packages, so a clause the engine's guard learns later is not learned here. **Accepted; drift risk noted; carrier none.**
- **F7 — filter-array spelling** (dev note): verified in the engine, ① 7. **Answered.**
- **F8 — #21080's finding (a)** (the snapshot redaction runs on find and findOne only, so a grouping carried the stored value): folded here — the `aggregate` op is guarded for all three members and the grouping refusal is pinned in the unit suites and on the real boot. **Closed by this PR.**
- **F9 — the approvals service door's own free-text rule (#11040) and the no-middleware-seam warning in `AuditPlugin`**: unchanged, as declared. **Answered.**
- **F10 — the PR body**: the seat appended the patch-round section and replaced the stale round-0 lines; the body as read on GitHub matches the diff and the two reports. **Answered.**
- **F11 — reviewer finding, the ledger list is unpinned**: `AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_GUARD.columns` restates `audit-log-field-redaction.ts`'s private constant and is held equal to it by nothing, where the activity list is pinned to its redaction's strip. Equal at this head; a later change to either list would go unmeasured. Not blocking. **For the seat to carry: a strip-equality pin in `audit-log-predicate-guard.test.ts`, mirroring the activity suite's.**
- **F12 — reviewer note, `details.reason`**: both guards reuse the predicate guard's reason for the aggregate role too; H5 pins code, status and first sentence, which match. **Noted, not blocking.**
- **F13 — reviewer note, census rows**: rows 17 and 45 carry behaviour prose beyond the anchor cells. Judged within the seat's Q2 — a row's behaviour columns describe its anchors — and the counts are the generator's. **Accepted.**
- **F14 — landing facts**: draft, auto-merge off, no governed-surface path (Governed Surface Queue Guard success), head repo equal to base repo, no `needs:contract-review` label on the PR. Landing is the owning seat's.
